summary: Scheduled usage snapshot and alerting oscillation caused by mixed retention-tier ingest leading to tracehook signature mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on an enterprise plan (BrightLayer Health) are seeing scheduled usage snapshots for a large dashboard return inconsistent heatmap tiles and duplicate/invalid tracehook links. At the same time, an alert attached to the same dashboard is flapping (TRIGGER -> OK -> TRIGGER) every 4-8 minutes during a ~6 hour window on 2026-03-01.

Impact:
- Multiple scheduled snapshots produced blank or partially populated tiles for a business-critical dashboard used for daily usage billing reconciliation.
- Alerts tied to the dashboard metric flapped, triggering downstream PagerDuty alerts and causing customer confusion.
- Tracehook links in the alert notifications sometimes point to a stale runId (expired token) and fail with 404 in the customer console.

Why this is high priority:
This affects billing-adjacent analytics and customer trust for enterprise usage reporting. The customer is on a monthly reconciliation cycle and cannot accept missing data or noisy alerts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer has a high-cardinality dashboard (dashboard id: DL-19804) with an ad-hoc rollup query over API route usage and a tracehook parameter included in the SELECT.
2) The dashboard is scheduled to snapshot every hour across a 7-day sliding window and sends an alert to a webhook + Slack destination when the 95th percentile of per-route latency exceeds threshold.
3) Trigger: perform bulk replay of traffic in the customer's onboarding namespace to generate a burst across multiple cardinalities for ~20 minutes.
4) Observe: scheduled snapshot job starts (scheduled job id: sj-7102). Within 1-2 snapshots, the resulting export contains missing heatmap buckets and the alert evaluation alternates between TRIGGER and OK.
5) Reproduce locally by replaying a smaller dataset against the ingest pipeline with retention-tier flag (fast-path: hot-store; background: compacted warm store) enabled.
logs:
- Alert eval logs (cloudwatch link): https://logs.redwood/prod/alert-evals/2026-03-01/sj-7102
- Scheduled job trace: sj-7102 -> run: run-2026-03-01T09:00Z -> archived-run-id: ar-2026-03-01-09Z
- Example failing tracehook URL from Slack: https://console.redwood/dashboards/DL-19804?tracehook=th_5f9d... -> returns 404 (expired run token)
- Ingest service offset logs show repeated 'retention-tier-resolve' warnings from 09:02-15:40 UTC: 
  * WARN ingest: retention-tier-resolve: key=org-734 route=/v1/embeddings prefix-cache-hit=false tier=warm resolve-time=182ms
  * INFO compactor: backfill-schedule started for namespace org-734 segment=2026-02-28
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Hypothesis A: Scheduled snapshot worker reads a mix of hot-store and warm-store partitions for the same time window; warm-store compaction has late-arriving records causing the snapshot to re-evaluate alert thresholds and regenerate tracehook tokens.
- Hypothesis B: Deduplication/dedupe-window in alerting service is interacting poorly with scheduled snapshot replays, causing duplicate evaluation runs and token regeneration.
- Hypothesis C: A bug in tracehook signing code produces non-deterministic tokens when the snapshot is run concurrently with a warm-store compaction job.

What we found so far:
- Correlated timestamps from ingest and snapshot workers show that when the compactor runs concurrently, the scheduled snapshot reads some partitions from hot-store and some from warm-store. Warm-store records for the same bucket were sometimes inserted ~30-120s after hot-store reads, which explains partial tiles.
- Alert evaluation engine started two separate evaluation transactions for the same scheduled job (eval-tx ids: etx-1249, etx-1250) spaced 5 minutes apart. etx-1250 had an updated token mapping table and generated new tracehook tokens; the alerting subsystem's dedupe logic allowed both transactions because the evaluation fingerprint changed due to late-arriving rows.
- Tracehook signing service logged rare HMAC context collisions when run concurrently under load; race window identified when signing key refresh coincides with token generation requests.

Intermediate mitigation applied (03-02):
- Paused scheduled snapshots for dashboard DL-19804 during the customer's reconciliation window.
- Implemented temporary rate-limit on compactor backfills for org-734 to reduce concurrent compaction during snapshot windows.
- Added a short buffer (30s) to snapshot worker to re-resolve partitions to prefer hot-store reads first.

Remaining unknowns:
- Whether dedupe logic should more aggressively coalesce evaluation transactions when identical scheduled_job ids are present.
- Whether a longer-term fix is needed in token signing to avoid HMAC collisions under concurrent key refresh.
comments: 2026-03-01 11:05 - Support (Aisha): Opened ticket after BrightLayer support request #4274 in Slack (#support-enterprise). Customer reports noisy alerts and missing tiles in hourly snapshots.

2026-03-01 13:20 - SRE (Rafael): Collected logs and correlated snapshot job with ingest compactor run. Noticed warm-store writes delayed by compactor and multiple eval transactions for the same snapshot job.

2026-03-02 09:45 - Engineering (Priya Desai): Reproduced locally with compactor backfill enabled; confirmed that mixed-store reads can produce partial buckets in snapshots. Filed PR to add pre-snapshot partition pinning (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5301).
2026-03-03 16:10 - Support (Aisha): Customer acknowledged temporary pause and accepted manual reconciliation for March 1st snapshots. Requested ETA for permanent fix and assurance no recurrence.
2026-03-04 08:32 - SRE (Rafael): Deployed temporary snapshot buffer (30s) and limited compactor concurrency for org-734. Observed no flapping events in the subsequent 24h window.

2026-03-05 10:15 - Engineering (Priya Desai): Investigating tracehook signing race; adding mutex around key-refresh + signing operation in signing-service. Will monitor HMAC collision logs for next 48h.
resolution:
Workaround and short-term mitigations applied: paused scheduled snapshots for the customer's reconciliation window, limited compactor concurrency for the org, and introduced a 30s pre-snapshot buffer to favor hot-store reads.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Console: implement partition pinning for scheduled snapshots to ensure a single storage tier is read per job (PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5301).
- Alerting: adjust dedupe logic to coalesce evaluation transactions for identical scheduled_job fingerprints within configurable window.
- Signing service: add lock around key refresh and token generation to eliminate rare HMAC context collisions (PR in progress).

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem due 2026-03-12 (confluence: /company/postmortems/SUP-999777).
- Customer success to schedule reconciliation call and provide CSV of corrected snapshot for March 1.
- Monitor incident metrics: alert-flap-count, snapshot-failure-rate for next 7 days.

Current status: In Progress (engineering PRs under review).
final_notes: This ticket spans ingest, retention, console snapshotting, alerting dedupe behavior, and signing service correctness. Recommend cross-team review at next SRE-ENG sync to align on partitioning guarantees for scheduled jobs.
